title: The Perfect Model

scenario.situation: A new churn prediction model just scored AUC 0.95 on the offline test set. The team is excited and wants to ship it to production next sprint.
scenario.stakeholderBelief: The DS manager argues the 0.95 AUC speaks for itself — this is the best model the team has ever built and any further delay costs the retention team a competitive edge.
scenario.question: Is this model actually ready to deploy?

decisions.prompt: Before signing off on deployment, how do you investigate whether the model's performance is trustworthy?

options.label: Benchmark against previous models
options.detail: Compare the 0.95 AUC to prior churn models to confirm the improvement is real.
options.consequence: The new model does beat prior models — but prior models were also trained on the same dataset with the same pipeline. If something is wrong with the data, every comparison is equally contaminated.
options.divergenceCost: Anchored on relative performance within a potentially flawed pipeline — contamination doesn't show up in peer comparisons.

options.label: Audit the feature set for data integrity
options.detail: Review every feature for its real-world availability at prediction time — can each variable actually be observed before a customer churns?
options.consequence: Walking through each feature's generation logic, you spot a flag called 'cancellation_request_submitted'. You trace it: it is written to the database only after a customer initiates a cancellation — after the outcome you are trying to predict. This single feature demands immediate scrutiny.

options.label: Tune the decision threshold for production
options.detail: Accept the model's quality and focus on finding the optimal precision/recall tradeoff for the retention team's workflow.
options.consequence: You produce a carefully tuned threshold, but the underlying AUC is what determines how much room threshold-tuning has to work with. If the AUC is artificial, threshold work is cosmetic.
options.divergenceCost: Jumped to operationalizing a result whose validity hadn't been confirmed — premature optimization.

options.label: Run a shadow deployment for two weeks
options.detail: Deploy in shadow mode alongside the existing system and compare live predictions to eventual outcomes.
options.consequence: Shadow deployment will eventually reveal the truth — but it takes weeks and could expose customers to a bad intervention strategy if the team acts on shadow scores. It also delays surfacing a problem that a quick data audit would catch today.
options.divergenceCost: Chose a slow live experiment when a preventable design flaw was detectable by inspection.

decisions.prompt: You've flagged 'cancellation_request_submitted' as suspicious. Which metric cut convinces you — and the manager — whether leakage is real?

artifact.title: Model AUC across evaluation splits
artifact.caption: Four AUC scores depending on split strategy and feature inclusion. Which comparison is actually valid?

options.label: AUC on a random train/test split with all features
options.detail: Use the standard holdout the team already ran — the 0.95 figure.
options.consequence: A random split mixes future information into training. Rows where 'cancellation_request_submitted' is TRUE will appear in both train and test, and the model has essentially memorized the answer. The 0.95 tells you nothing about real-world predictive power.
options.divergenceCost: Trusted a split that leaks the outcome across train and test sets — the contamination is invisible in the number itself.

options.label: AUC on a time-respecting split with the suspicious feature removed
options.detail: Re-evaluate using only data available before the churn event, train on earlier months, test on the most recent month, and exclude 'cancellation_request_submitted'.
options.consequence: The model drops to AUC 0.61 — barely above a naive baseline of 0.60. The 34-point gap between 0.95 and 0.61 is entirely explained by a single leaky feature. The manager can now see the gap in a single chart rather than debate it abstractly.

artifact.title: AUC: leaky random split vs. leakage-free temporal split
artifact.caption: Only the temporal, leakage-free split reflects production reality. The model collapses to near-baseline once the future-derived flag is removed and time ordering is respected.

decisions.prompt: The leakage-free AUC is 0.61. What do you tell the DS manager?

options.label: "The model is broken — we need to start over."
options.detail: Frame the finding as a failure and recommend rebuilding from scratch.
options.consequence: This is technically warranted but framed unproductively. It doesn't tell the manager what to do next, doesn't acknowledge that remaining features may still carry real signal, and risks triggering a defensive reaction that buries the finding.
options.divergenceCost: Overclaimed a complete failure without charting a constructive path — accurate finding, poor analytical communication.

options.label: "The 0.95 is driven by a single leaky feature. The leakage-free model sits at 0.61 — real but modest. We should rebuild with a temporal split policy, drop the flag, and re-evaluate before any deployment decision."
options.detail: Name the specific cause, quantify the real performance, and recommend a concrete remediation path.
options.consequence: The manager now has the precise diagnosis, a comparable honest baseline, and an actionable next step. The team avoids deploying a model that would silently fail in production — where 'cancellation_request_submitted' will never be available at prediction time.

insight: The model's 0.95 AUC was almost entirely explained by 'cancellation_request_submitted' — a flag written to the database only after a customer decides to leave, making it a direct encoding of the outcome rather than a predictor of it. A random train/test split cannot detect this because leaky rows appear on both sides; only a temporally ordered, leakage-free split exposes the collapse. The lesson is that outstanding offline metrics should trigger scrutiny, not confidence: always audit features for temporal availability and validate with splits that mirror the production timeline.
